requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) permits node3->node4 TCP/23 traffic and records (logs) it
requirements.summary: VyOS forward filter rule 10 was committed and saved with action accept, protocol tcp, destination port 23, log enabled, inbound eth2/outbound eth1 (node3-facing to node2-facing). `show configuration commands` confirms the persisted rule, and `show log firewall` shows repeated ACCEPT ([ipv4-FWD-filter-10-A]) entries with SRC=10.10.12.1 DST=10.10.34.2 DPT=23 matching the configured flow.

requirements.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) refuses node3->node4 TCP/23 traffic and records (logs) the refusal
requirements.summary: A block+log filter rule for tcp/23 on opt1 (vtnet1, the node1-facing link) was added to config.xml and applied via configctl filter reload; pfctl -sr confirms 'block drop in log quick on vtnet1 inet proto tcp ... port = telnet'. The filter log (filter_20260906.log) shows matching 'block,in,vtnet1' entries for the exact same flow (SRC=10.10.12.1 DST=10.10.34.2, DPT=23).

requirements.requirement: A single connection attempt from node3 produces a matching permit(node1)/refuse(node2) log pair from which the stopping point is evident
requirements.summary: One nc attempt from node3 at 2026-09-06T04:29:22Z timed out (cmd-c927889471dc42ae). node1's firewall log shows ACCEPT entries at 00:29:22 local with IP ID=26369/26370, SPT=52186, DPT=23 (cmd-1db697f731e64edd); node2's filter log shows block entries for the identical packet (same IP ID, source port, and TCP ISN=2246665030) at 04:29:22 UTC (cmd-62d843bef32e498d). The matching identifiers directly establish that the same packet was passed by node1 and stopped at node2.

requirements.requirement: End-to-end permit/refuse behavior and matching log pairing survive all four node restarts
requirements.summary: Post-restart nc attempt at 2026-09-06T04:31:37Z timed out (cmd-c9499f2d88b24d6b). node1 log shows ACCEPT with IP ID=39799, SPT=60700, DPT=23 (cmd-778ad28d97674e35); node2 log shows block for the identical packet (same IP ID, ports, ISN=3989428445) at the same timestamp (cmd-d7c0240d32f34249), confirming the behavior and its log evidence remained intact after all restarts.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 permits and logs the node3->node4 tcp/23 flow, node2 refuses and logs the same flow, and a single nc attempt from node3 produced a directly correlated permit(node1)/refuse(node2) log pair (matching IP ID, ports, and TCP ISN) that unambiguously shows the traffic passed node1 and was stopped at node2. The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also completed and well-documented for all four nodes: each shows a pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged restart, a changed boot identity (or FreeBSD boottime), and recovered interface/route/firewall configuration, with the end-to-end permit/refuse log-pairing behavior re-verified and shown intact after all four restarts.
limitations: Boot-identity and behavioral verification rely on the executor's own captured command outputs rather than an independent verifier probe, though these are corroborated by the fixed before/after lifecycle snapshots.

The pcap/tcpdump diagnostic artifacts and some /tmp scratch files from troubleshooting were not directly confirmed as deleted, though the subsequent reboots (tmpfs reset on VyOS/OPNsense/AlmaLinux private tmp) appear to have cleared them per the after_executor temp-file listings.

The OPNsense static route and gateway entries were injected via direct XML manipulation with a python script rather than the GUI/API; functional correctness was confirmed via pfctl/netstat/ifconfig output but the long-term maintainability of this method versus GUI-driven configuration was not assessed.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's state-changing commands are traceable to the task's material outcomes or the mandated restart protocol: interface/route configuration on all four nodes, VyOS firewall rule commits, OPNsense config.xml edits + reconfigure/reload calls, and the four node reboots. An initial wrong interface-swap assumption on node1 was corrected in a later config session (cmd-f93bfedcc57149b0) rather than left broken -- a legitimate corrective action, not residue. `dnf install -y nc` on node3 and node4 (cmd-edb88769d3dd4aac, cmd-4c2bb886b5784586) and a persistent `ncat` listener left running on node4:23 (visible in after_executor listening-sockets) are minor retained additions, but both are directly required to give the flow a real telnet-port destination and a client tool for the mandated demonstration, so they are not unnecessary mutations. Diagnostic commands (tcpdump, arping, ping, config template exploration) were read-only or self-bounded and largely cleared naturally by the subsequent reboots (tmpfs reset), as shown by the before/after temp-file diffs. No failed services, no package-manager inconsistency, and no unsafe exposure were introduced on any node per the fixed lifecycle snapshots.
